doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: What R&B gigs paid
summary: Grimes recalls that R&B pay such as with Willis Jackson was the most money he had made.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Henry, can you remember what some of those rhythm & blues gigs would have paid at the time?
Well I almost forgot totally what I got paid. But it was very uplifting I remember, to get paid, because it was the most money I ever made in my life you know.
Whatever it was it was the most you made.

Yeah. It was the most money I ever made. And I mean a lot of it was left over and whenever they kept the money, but I mean, but it was, for instance, a musician like Willis Jackson, you could play with him and get that amount of money, so it was pretty cool.
And, you know anybody like that, the pay is cool.
Yeah. That’s a good feeling to like get paid for something that you’re loving, right?
That you like to do, yeah. Yeah, it always amazed me when I got money for doing that. It always did.
